title: When Will The Benchmaxxing Plague End? — Nick Heiner, Surge AI
talk_summary: Nick Heiner argues benchmarks are systematically gamed and misaligned with real-world value due to cost, contamination, reward hacking, and sloppy verifiers, and that the fix is expert-built tasks with verifiers fully aligned to prompts plus private holdout sets.

takeaways.what_they_do: They require that every requirement in a task prompt is checked by the verifier and every verifier check corresponds to something the prompt actually asks for, treating either mismatch as unfair noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the verifiers need to be verifying everything the prompt asks for. And everything the prompt asks for needs to be covered by the verifiers

takeaways.technique: Adversarial reward-hacking pass on the reviewer
takeaways.what_they_do: They design verifiers assuming a maximally lazy agent will find the letter-of-the-law shortcut, so graders must be robust to that.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need to think about designing your rewards as a adversarial process against this maximally lazy agent.

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a private holdout set so the benchmark isn't contaminated and so saturation reflects real capability, not memorization.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to have a private hold out set so you don't get contaminated

takeaways.what_they_do: They show a benchmark where a strong and weak model both score 20% because the verifier only accepts one of many valid formats, so the task can't distinguish models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the benchmark task is not differentiating between Haiku and Fable, it's not a useful task.

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue synthetic data introduces eval-awareness and out-of-distribution noise, and that high-fidelity input data should come from the real world.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Synthetic approaches are possible, but it is very very hard to do it reliably.

takeaways.technique: Expert-authored task specs, not AI-generated ones
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist task definitions, success criteria, inputs, and tools come from domain experts with product sense, because AI-generated specs can't push the frontier.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't push the frontier forward from within the frontier
